route: The flip graph of realised one-player orientations: prove the single-edge-reversal criterion, prove that a drive line of a readout system is a walk in that graph, then use the walk at m=6 and the resulting classification of ties at m=5.
object: W_m, the realisation graph: the induced subgraph, on the improvement outmaps of nondegenerate one-player stopping SSGs with m Max vertices, of the flip graph F_m in which two acyclic unique sink orientations of the m-cube are adjacent when they differ in the direction of exactly one cube edge — together with the drive lines (continuous paths in the space of readout systems) whose fences are its edges.
headline: No stopping SSG with Vmin empty and |Vmax| = 5 has an all-switches run of length 12, degenerate or not, so h*_1(5) = h*_1^nd(5) = h*_LP(5) = h*_HK(5) = 11.

results.name: mw:flip — the single-edge reversal criterion
results.statement: Let s be a unique sink orientation of the m-cube, u' = u ⊕ e_i, and let t be s with the edge {u,u'} reversed. (a) t is a unique sink orientation iff s(u) ⊕ s(u') = e_i, i.e. iff u ⊕ s(u) = u' ⊕ s(u') (the endpoints share a bottom-antipodal successor). (b) When it holds, t = s∘(u u'); every other vertex keeps its bottom-antipodal successor while u and u' acquire the common successor z ⊕ e_i (z their common successor in s); the sink stays put unless it is an endpoint, when it crosses the edge. (c) Acyclicity is a separate condition: if s is acyclic and t is a unique sink orientation, t is acyclic iff s has no directed path from the tail of {u,u'} to its head other than the edge itself — and this can fail, e.g. s = (0,1,3,2,6,5,4,7) on the 3-cube with the edge {1,5} in direction 2, whose reversal t = (0,5,3,2,6,1,4,7) is a cyclic unique sink orientation.
results.why_not_implied: rem:pinned-escape asserts the same equivalence but only as an exhaustive machine check at m ≤ 3, with no proof and no acyclicity clause; a verification at m ≤ 3 gives nothing at m ≥ 4, and the paper's own walk searches at m = 4,5,6 run on it.
results.argument: Sufficiency: assume s(u)⊕s(u') = e_i, so t swaps the outmap values of u and u'. Check the Szabó–Welzl condition pairwise. Only pairs (u,y) and (u',y) with y outside the edge need work. With d := s(u')⊕s(y): if i ∉ u'⊕y then u⊕y ⊇ u'⊕y and the condition for s at (u',y) transfers; if i ∈ u'⊕y then u⊕y = (u'⊕y)\{i}, and if d∩(u⊕y) were empty then d∩(u'⊕y) = {i}, whence (s(u)⊕s(y))∩(u⊕y) = (d⊕e_i)∩(u⊕y) = d∩(u⊕y) = ∅, contradicting the condition for s at (u,y). Necessity: if j ≠ i lies in s(u)⊕s(u'), restrict to the 2-face F on directions i,j through u (restrictions of unique sink orientations to faces are unique sink orientations). Exactly one of the two j-edges of F points up; then F has a unique sink iff exactly one of 'u→u'' and 'b→a' holds, and reversing {u,u'} negates that exclusive disjunction, so s|F and t|F cannot both be unique sink orientations. (b) is a direct computation. (c) t minus the reversed edge equals s minus it, hence is acyclic, so every cycle of t uses the reversed edge.
results.verification: Exhaustive at m ≤ 3, exact and combinatorial (flipcrit.py, acyc_cex.py): over all 744 unique sink orientations of the 3-cube and all 8928 single-edge reversals, the criterion agrees with the unique sink property in every case (0 mismatches); the transposition clause t = s∘(u u') and the path characterisation of acyclicity hold in every case; and exactly 48 of the reversals turn an acyclic orientation into a cyclic one, the first being the printed example. At m = 2 the same test over all 12 unique sink orientations and 48 reversals: 0 mismatches, 0 acyclicity failures.

results.name: mw:cells and mw:monotone — a drive line is a walk in the flip graph, and a monotone drive line is a geodesic
results.statement: Let Σ_{m,δ} be the polytope of δ-leaky reduced one-player readout systems and g(σ,v) the gap of the incidence (σ,v). (mw:tie-edge) g(σ,v) = 0 iff x_σ = x_{σ⊕e_v} iff g(σ⊕e_v,v) = 0, and otherwise the two gaps have opposite signs: ties are an EDGE phenomenon. (mw:cells) Along a drive line (a rational path in Σ_{m,δ}) no gap of which vanishes identically, the fence set is finite of size at most (m+1)m2^{m-1}; the outmap is constant on each cell and lies in R_m; at a simple fence the two adjacent cells' outmaps differ exactly in the reversal of the tied edge; hence if all fences are simple the cell outmaps form a walk in W_m and the number of fences is at least |Δ(s(0),s(1))|. (mw:monotone) If the affine drive line moves only one row, or moves only the constant terms q with all p fixed (the driven-block shape), then every gap is a quotient of two affine functions of t with non-vanishing denominator — affine outright in the second case — so each edge of the cube is tied at most once, there are at most m2^{m-1} fences, and if all are simple their number is EXACTLY |Δ(s(0),s(1))|: the walk is a geodesic of F_m and no edge is reversed twice.
results.why_not_implied: prop:pinned-level computes the outmap of a driven block at given drive values for one particular shape; it says nothing about how the outmap changes as the drive moves — not that a fence reverses exactly one edge, not that each edge ties at most once, not that the fence count equals the flip distance, and it does not produce a walk in any graph.
results.argument: mw:tie-edge: a vanishing gap makes x_σ a fixed point of the σ[v]-system, so x_{σ[v]} = x_σ by uniqueness of the contraction's fixed point, whence the partner gap vanishes too; strict signs follow from monotone policy improvement applied in both directions. mw:cells: by Cramer, det(I−P_σ(t)) has degree ≤ m and never vanishes on [0,1], and each gap is a polynomial of degree ≤ m+1 over it; off the fences all signs are locally constant; the realising conditions are strict inequalities, so a cell contains dyadic δ/2-leaky systems and thm:readout-realise(b) applies; at a simple fence only the two gaps of one edge change sign, which is that edge's reversal, and both cell outmaps are AUSOs by prop:allsw-auso so mw:flip(a) applies. mw:monotone: in the q-case I−P_σ is constant, so x_σ(t) is affine; in the one-row case only one row of I−P_σ(t) and of q_σ(t) moves, so expanding along it makes both Cramer determinants affine, while every alternative row is constant — so each gap is a Möbius function of t and has at most one zero.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic throughout (exactline.py, qline_test.py, rowline_test.py, rowline_fences.py, qline6.py). On the 260-vertex height-11 five-state witness of prop:hstar-one-eleven: twelve q-lines, every gap verified affine in t at seven sample points, fences 41,35,62,59,59,55,31,35,58,30,49,45 — all simple, every step a single-edge reversal satisfying mw:flip(a), no edge reversed twice, every cell an AUSO, and the fence count equal to |Δ(s(0),s(1))| in every case. Six one-row lines out of the same system: the Möbius property verified by the vanishing of the 4×4 determinant of the rows (1,t,g,tg) at four points for all 160 incidences; fences located by 60-step bisection are pairwise distinct, hence all simple, and number exactly |Δ| = 6,5,5,16,12,28. Re-run on the fresh and larger 418-vertex six-state witness of mw:h13: six q-lines with 83,106,149,107,83,117 fences against the ceiling m2^{m−1} = 192, all simple, all single-edge reversals meeting the criterion, no edge twice, every cell an AUSO of height 3 to 13, fence count = |Δ| in every case.

results.name: mw:drive-return and mw:b2-return — a one-player driven block never returns, and the level-two block does
results.statement: (mw:drive-return) If the readouts of a block B of Max vertices, in the game with a vertex β pinned at θ, form a one-player readout system whose coefficients on the B-values are θ-independent and whose constants move affinely with θ, then along the whole drive line every edge of the |B|-cube ties at most once, so the block's orientation performs a walk in the flip graph that reverses no edge twice and NEVER RETURNS to an orientation it has left; the line has at most |B|2^{|B|−1} fences. (mw:b2-return) The level-two block of prop:b2-realised (Max c1,c2,c3 with the Min vertex c6, driven by θ = y_{c5}) has on [0,1] exactly the 14 cells and 13 fences of rem:pinned-escape, all simple; the 13 reversed edges are, in order, (4,β1),(3,β1),(0,seed),(0,β1),(1,β1),(2,β1),(4,seed),(0,α1),(3,β1),(1,α1),(6,seed),(2,seed),(5,α1); the edge {3,7} in the direction β1 is reversed TWICE, and the flip distance between the first and the last cell is 11 against 13 fences. So the block is not a one-player driven block. This is invisible cell by cell: all fourteen cell outmaps are Holt-Klee, of heights 4,3,2,1,2,2,2,3,4,3,3,2,2,3, so each of them separately is realisable by a nondegenerate one-player game (prop:m3-realised) and thm:min-count demands nothing at any single drive value; what forces the Min vertex is the return.
results.why_not_implied: thm:min-count bounds k below by log2 of the Holt-Klee defect of the realised outmap; here every one of the fourteen outmaps the block presents is Holt-Klee, so thm:min-count gives k ≥ 0 at every drive value and cannot see the Min vertex at all — the obstruction is the pair of drive values at which the same edge is oriented one way, then the other, then back.
results.argument: mw:drive-return is mw:monotone case (ii): the gaps are affine in θ, an edge is tied where either of its gaps vanishes, an affine function has at most one zero unless identically zero, and reversing an edge twice would need two ties on it. For mw:b2-return the block system with y_{c5} substituted is a 4×4 linear fixed point whose matrix is θ-independent and whose right-hand side is affine in θ, one system per Min action, and val_σ is the componentwise minimum of the two solutions (cor:comparison) — so each block value is a minimum of two affine functions of θ and each gap is piecewise affine with at most two pieces, which is exactly the room the extra reversal needs. Twelve edges of the 3-cube against thirteen fences forces a repetition; the computation names it.
results.verification: From the game, in exact rational arithmetic. b2fromgame.py loads the 138-vertex game file of prop:b2-realised (5 Max, 1 Min, 130 average) and recomputes the first-passage law of every controlled action onto C ∪ {t1} by solving the 130×130 rational absorption system with C and the sinks absorbing; the result is exactly the printed harmonic normal form. b2drive.py then scans the drive line on the grid θ ∈ (1/4000)Z ∩ [0,1], finding 14 cells and 13 transitions, with outmap B^1 = (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2) on the first cell and B^1(·⊕e_{β1}) = (7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6) on the ninth, matching rem:b2-anatomy. b2fences.py then confirms EXACTLY, at each of the thirteen rationals printed in rem:pinned-escape, that some gap vanishes there and that the outmap differs on the two sides; each falls in a distinct grid interval, so the correspondence is one-to-one and every fence is simple. Each transition reverses exactly one edge, each satisfying mw:flip(a); the reversal counts per edge are all 1 except (3,β1), which is 2. All fourteen cell outmaps were tested Holt-Klee by the unit-vertex-capacity max-flow test.

results.name: mw:no-twelve — one player cannot reach twelve at m = 5, with or without ties
results.statement: No stopping SSG with Vmin = ∅ and |Vmax| = 5 has an all-switches run of length 12, degenerate or not. Hence h*_1(5) = h*_1^nd(5) = h*_LP(5) = h*_HK(5) = 11 < 12 = h*(5), and the one-player row of rem:four-ceilings reads 1,2,4,6,11 for m ≤ 5. The supporting lemma mw:twelve-flat: there are exactly 480 acyclic unique sink orientations of the 5-cube whose bottom-antipodal walk from 0 has length 12 and none of length 13, so up to translation these are all the height-12 orientations; exactly 240 of them admit a partition into subcubes satisfying (F1)-(F4) of lem:seven-flat with a block of dimension ≥ 1, and in every such case the partition is unique, its only nontrivial block is the single edge {σ0, σ0 ⊕ e_x} at the start, and the run carries exactly one flat incidence, (σ0,x); the five values of x occur 48 times each.
results.why_not_implied: thm:no-seven settles m = 4 only, and the paragraph after prop:hkfive settles just the one named height-12 class s_12 of the 5-cube while asserting that the other height-12 classes 'cannot be enumerated'; the case m = 5 is stated there as open (rem:four-ceilings: 'whether h*_1 ≤ h*_HK is the question left open after thm:no-seven, settled there for m ≤ 4 only').
results.argument: Let G be such a game with run σ0,…,σ12. Its run vertices lie in pairwise distinct flat classes (lem:flat-class(c)), so setting the corners on the run and applying thm:flat-resolution gives a resolution s' whose bottom-antipodal walk from σ0 is the run (cor:ceiling-general); its height is ≥ 12, hence = 12 because h*(5) = 12; translating by σ0 puts it among the 480. The flat partition of G satisfies (F1) because s' = S_A ∪ (σ ⊕ c_A) on a class, (F2) because S and D are disjoint, (F3) by lem:flat-class(c), (F4) by lem:face-sink. By mw:twelve-flat either G is nondegenerate or its only nontrivial flat class is the starting edge and the run carries exactly one flat incidence; in both cases cor:one-tie and lem:tie-perturb produce a generic linear functional on the occupancy polytope whose orientation is Holt-Klee on every face and whose bottom-antipodal walk from σ0 is the run, so 12 ≤ h*_HK(5) = 11 (prop:hkfive), a contradiction. The equalities then follow from h*_1^nd ≤ h*_LP ≤ h*_HK (prop:oneplayer-lp), h*_HK(5) = 11 (prop:hkfive) and the nondegenerate height-11 witness of prop:hstar-one-eleven.
results.verification: Exact and combinatorial. h12b.c enumerates, by depth-first search over the walk pruned by cor:no-return, cor:law-b and the Szabó–Welzl condition among assigned vertices (outmaps of unique sink orientations being bijections), followed by a bijective completion of the remaining 19 vertices and an acyclicity test: at m = 5, length 12 it returns exactly 480 orientations in 1.2 s, at length 13 exactly 0 (reproducing h*(5) = 12 independently), and at m = 4, length 7 exactly the 48 orientations of lem:seven-flat with σ0 = 0 (i.e. its 768 pairs), which validates the program against the paper. All 480 were re-checked here to be unique sink orientations, acyclic, of height 12, and NONE Holt-Klee by the unit-vertex-capacity max-flow test, reproducing prop:hkfive. flatpart.py enumerates, for each of the 480, the candidate blocks (subcubes on which σ ↦ σ ⊕ s(σ) is constant, which is (F1)) and all exact covers by them, testing (F2)-(F4); rerun at m = 4 it returns lem:seven-flat verbatim (24 of the 48, one partition each, the edge {0,e_x} at the start, one flat incidence (0,x)). At m = 5 it returns 240 of the 480, each with exactly one nontrivial admissible partition, in every case the edge {0, e_x} with x uniform over the five coordinates (48 each) and the single run tie (t,v,a) = (0,x,0).

results.name: mw:h13 — h*_1^nd(6) ≥ 13, and the stacking slope rises to 13/7
results.statement: There is a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG on 418 vertices (6 Max, 410 average, two sinks), of harmonic normal form denominator 2^14, whose improvement orientation is a Holt-Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the 6-cube of bottom-antipodal height 13, with the all-switches run 25,14,33,6,37,46,45,44,16,40,0,8,28,12 and switched sets {0,1,2,4},{0,1,2,3,5},{0,1,2,5},{0,1,5},{0,1,3},{0,1},{0},{2,3,4,5},{3,4,5},{3,5},{3},{2,4},{4}. Hence h*_1(6) ≥ h*_1^nd(6) ≥ 13 and h*_LP(6) ≥ 13, improving both entries ≥ 12 of rem:four-ceilings; with prop:oneplayer-plus-one, h*_1(7) ≥ 14, h*_LP(7) ≥ 14 and h*_1(m) ≥ m + 7 for m ≥ 6 (so h*_1(8) ≥ 15, superseding prop:hstar-one-eight); and with cor:stack-family at m2 = 6, h*_1(7k−1) ≥ 13k for every k and liminf_m h*_1(m)/m ≥ 13/7 > 11/6.
results.why_not_implied: prop:hstar-one-eleven settles m = 5 (h*_1^nd(5) = 11) and rem:hk-survey records explicitly that the same route's walk towards a Holt-Klee height-13 class of the 6-cube 'was cut short by its budget: h*_1(6) ≥ 13 and the one-player doubling remain open'; no chaining of the paper's laws gives 13 at m = 6 (prop:oneplayer-plus-one gives 12, cor:stack-family gives at most 11).
results.argument: The system was found by a guided walk in W_6 of the kind mw:cells licenses: from the round-18 realised height-12 orientation, the criterion neighbours of mw:flip(a) that are acyclic and Holt-Klee were ordered by outmap distance to a target and the first that a warm-started optimisation over the 72 row parameters re-realised was taken; the target was produced combinatorially by a best-first search in the Holt-Klee part of F_6, which reached a height-13 orientation after 569 expansions along 32 flips. The height-13 system appeared after six realised steps. The lower bounds then follow from prop:oneplayer-lp (a nondegenerate one-player improvement orientation is an LP orientation), prop:oneplayer-plus-one and cor:stack-family's h*_1(m1+m2+1) ≥ h*_1(m1) + h*_1^nd(m2) with liminf ≥ sup_{m0} h*_1^nd(m0)/(m0+1).
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic, from the game (verify13.py on H13_m6_WITNESS_GAME.json). The game is one-player (6 max, 410 avg, 0 min), every non-sink has out-degree two, its greatest trap is empty so it is stopping (lem:trapchar). Its average part is acyclic, so every vertex is a substochastic affine function of the six Max values, computed twice by independent code paths (topological order in gameeval.py and memoised recursion) and equal in both to the printed dyadic rows; every row leaks, least leak 5/16384, and p^{v,a}_v = 0 throughout. The 64 value vectors, from 64 exact 6×6 rational systems, give the recorded outmap with NO tied incidence, least margin 226793593012712537793143/3187971438880543888553754624 (the same number is produced independently by occ_exact.check run on the printed system). The outmap is a unique sink orientation, acyclic, and Holt-Klee by the unit-vertex-capacity max-flow test; its bottom-antipodal height is 13, attained at the four strategies 25,27,57,59, and the longest all-switches run over all 64 starts is 13. The run was recomputed by applying the all-switches rule itself from the game — comparing the two actions under val_σ at each strategy — and coincides with the bottom-antipodal walk; the value vector is nondecreasing at every vertex along it and strictly increasing somewhere at each of the 13 rounds. Search state: 475 distinct realised height-13 orientations reached; among the 14957 acyclic criterion neighbours of 329 of them none has height 14 (neighbour heights 8:4, 9:163, 10:339, 11:1767, 12:2107, 13:10577), and over all 475 none of the 1.1×10^6 orientations at flip distance two has height 14 either.

results.name: mw:w3 — the realisation graph is connected at m = 3
results.statement: R_3 is exactly the set of Holt-Klee acyclic unique sink orientations of the 3-cube, 656 of the 728 acyclic ones, and W_3 = F_3[R_3] is connected, of minimum degree 3, maximum degree 12 and average degree 5.41; the flip graph F_3 of all 728 is connected as well.
results.why_not_implied: prop:m3-realised says every class at m = 3 is realised; it says nothing about adjacency between realised orientations, which is a statement about the graph structure this route introduces and which is what makes a walk a proof device rather than a heuristic.
results.argument: R_3 = the Holt-Klee AUSOs of the 3-cube by prop:oneplayer-lp (only Holt-Klee ones are realised by nondegenerate one-player games) together with prop:m3-realised (every Holt-Klee class is realised); the adjacency is given by mw:flip, and connectivity is then a finite check.
results.verification: w3.py: all 728 acyclic unique sink orientations of the 3-cube enumerated by brute force, 656 found Holt-Klee by the unit-vertex-capacity max-flow test, neighbours generated by the criterion of mw:flip and filtered for acyclicity; a union-find/DFS over both vertex sets returns one component of size 728 and one of size 656 respectively, with the stated degree statistics; the heights present in W_3 are 1,2,3,4.

gap: The connectivity of W_m for m ≥ 4 is not proved. What is missing is exactly this transversality statement: for a dense set of pairs (Ψ_0, Ψ_1) of nondegenerate systems in the polytope Σ_{m,δ}, the segment from Ψ_0 to Ψ_1 meets no two of the degeneracy hypersurfaces {g(σ,v) = 0} at the same parameter. (Each such hypersurface is smooth, since ∂g(σ,v)/∂q^{v,1−σ(v)} = 1 identically, and Σ_{m,δ} is convex, so this is the only step between what is proved here and 'W_m is connected'.) Also unsettled: whether the doubling of thm:blowup at the step 4 → 6 is realised by one player, i.e. whether the height-14 Holt-Klee orientation s_6 of prop:hk-records is in R_6.
next_steps: (1) Prove the transversality statement above; it would give W_m connected and make the guided walk complete rather than merely sound. (2) Resume the height-14 hunt from h13_states.json (475 realised height-13 orientations with their float systems, in the r3_*/r4_* logs of the code directory): every one of them is at flip distance ≥ 3 from height 14, so a two- or three-step lookahead, or a combinatorial best-first path to a height-14 Holt-Klee orientation followed step by step, is the way in; s_6 itself sits at 24 cube edges from the height-13 witness after the best of the 46080 automorphisms. (3) Push mw:no-twelve to m = 6: the method needs all AUSOs of the 6-cube of height ≥ h*(6), which is not enumerable by walk-then-complete, so a new idea is required — but the pattern at m = 4 and m = 5 (the only tie a maximal run can carry sits on one edge at the start) is worth trying to prove in general. (4) Apply mw:drive-return to the escape route of cor:escape-m3: a one-player driven block cannot present B^2 at one drive and return, which restricts which of the surviving corners can be one-player. (5) The 162 unresolved Holt-Klee classes of the 4-cube (rem:hk-survey) are now exactly the vertices of F_4 no walk in W_4 has reached; test whether they are cut off in F_4 restricted to Holt-Klee orientations, or merely missed.

\begin{definition}[The flip graph and the realisation graph]\label{mw:def-graph}
Let $\mathcal F_m$ be the graph whose vertices are the acyclic unique sink
orientations of the $m$-cube and whose edges join two orientations differing
in the direction of exactly one edge of the cube; write $d_{\mathrm{flip}}$
for its graph distance and, for two outmaps $s,t$, $\Delta(s,t)$ for the set
of cube edges on which they differ, so that
$d_{\mathrm{flip}}(s,t)\ge|\Delta(s,t)|$. Let $\mathcal R_m$ be the set of
improvement orientations (\Cref{def:improvement-uso}) of nondegenerate
one-player stopping SSGs with $|\Vmax|=m$ --- equivalently, by
\Cref{thm:readout-realise}, of dyadic $\delta$-leaky readout systems of order
$(m,1)$ --- and let $W_m:=\mathcal F_m[\mathcal R_m]$ be the induced subgraph:
the \emph{realisation graph}.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The single-edge reversal criterion]\label{mw:flip}
Let $s$ be a unique sink orientation of the $m$-cube, let $i<m$, let
$u\in\{0,1\}^m$, $u':=u\oplus e_i$, and let $t$ be $s$ with the edge
$\{u,u'\}$ reversed, that is
$t(u)=s(u)\oplus e_i$, $t(u')=s(u')\oplus e_i$ and $t=s$ elsewhere.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $t$ is a unique sink orientation if and only if
      $s(u)\oplus s(u')=e_i$, that is if and only if
      $u\oplus s(u)=u'\oplus s(u')$: the two endpoints of the reversed edge
      have the same bottom-antipodal successor.
\item When the criterion holds, $t=s\circ(u\,u')$, the transposition of the
      two endpoints; the bottom-antipodal successor of every vertex other
      than $u,u'$ is unchanged, while $u$ and $u'$ acquire the common
      successor $z\oplus e_i$, $z$ being their common successor under $s$;
      and the sink of $t$ is that of $s$ unless the latter is an endpoint of
      the reversed edge, in which case it moves to the other endpoint.
\item Acyclicity is a further, independent condition: if $s$ is acyclic and
      $t$ is a unique sink orientation, then $t$ is acyclic if and only if
      the only directed $s$-path from the tail of $\{u,u'\}$ to its head is
      the edge itself. It can fail: on the $3$-cube the acyclic unique sink
      orientation $s=(0,1,3,2,6,5,4,7)$ and the edge $\{1,5\}$ in direction
      $2$ satisfy the criterion, and the reversal
      $t=(0,5,3,2,6,1,4,7)$ is a \emph{cyclic} unique sink orientation.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(a) \emph{Sufficiency.} Assume $s(u)\oplus s(u')=e_i$, so $t(u)=s(u')$ and
$t(u')=s(u)$, which is (b)'s first clause. We verify the Szab\'o--Welzl
condition $(t(x)\oplus t(y))\cap(x\oplus y)\ne\emptyset$ for all $x\ne y$.
For $x,y\notin\{u,u'\}$ nothing changed. For $\{x,y\}=\{u,u'\}$,
$t(u)\oplus t(u')=e_i=u\oplus u'$. Let then $x=u$ and $y\notin\{u,u'\}$, and
put $d:=t(u)\oplus t(y)=s(u')\oplus s(y)$. If $i\notin u'\oplus y$ then
$u\oplus y=(u'\oplus y)\cup\{i\}\supseteq u'\oplus y$, and
$d\cap(u'\oplus y)\ne\emptyset$ because $s$ is a unique sink orientation, so
$d\cap(u\oplus y)\ne\emptyset$. If $i\in u'\oplus y$ then
$u\oplus y=(u'\oplus y)\setminus\{i\}$; suppose $d\cap(u\oplus y)=\emptyset$.
Then $d\cap(u'\oplus y)\subseteq\{i\}$ and, being nonempty, equals $\{i\}$.
But $s(u)\oplus s(y)=d\oplus e_i$ and $i\notin u\oplus y$, so
$(s(u)\oplus s(y))\cap(u\oplus y)=d\cap(u\oplus y)=\emptyset$, contradicting
the unique sink condition for $s$ at the pair $(u,y)$. The case $x=u'$ is
symmetric.

\emph{Necessity.} Suppose $j\ne i$ lies in $s(u)\oplus s(u')$ and let $F$ be
the $2$-face spanned by the directions $i,j$ through $u$; write its vertices
$u$, $u'=u\oplus e_i$, $a:=u\oplus e_j$, $b:=u'\oplus e_j$. The restriction
of a unique sink orientation to a face with free set $J$ is one --- for
$x,y$ in the face, $x\oplus y\subseteq J$, so
$((s(x)\cap J)\oplus(s(y)\cap J))\cap(x\oplus y)=(s(x)\oplus s(y))\cap(x\oplus y)\ne\emptyset$
--- so $s|_F$ is a unique sink orientation of the square, and so is $t|_F$ if
$t$ is one. By hypothesis
exactly one of the two $j$-edges $\{u,a\}$, $\{u',b\}$ points towards
$j$-level $1$; say $u\to a$ and $b\to u'$ (the other case is the same with
$u$ and $u'$ exchanged). Then $u$ is a sink of $F$ never, $b$ never; $a$ is a
sink of $F$ iff $b\to a$, and $u'$ is a sink of $F$ iff $u\to u'$. So $F$ has
exactly one sink iff exactly one of ``$u\to u'$'' and ``$b\to a$'' holds; and
reversing the edge $\{u,u'\}$ turns that exclusive disjunction into its
negation. Hence $s|_F$ and $t|_F$ cannot both be unique sink orientations.

(b) The identification $t=s\circ(u\,u')$ is immediate. For $x\notin\{u,u'\}$
nothing changed. With $z:=u\oplus s(u)=u'\oplus s(u')$ one computes
$u\oplus t(u)=u\oplus s(u)\oplus e_i=z\oplus e_i$ and
$u'\oplus t(u')=u'\oplus s(u')\oplus e_i=z\oplus e_i$. The sink clause is
$t(x)=0\Leftrightarrow s(x)=0$ for $x\notin\{u,u'\}$, and
$t(u)=s(u')$, $t(u')=s(u)$.

(c) Deleting the edge $\{u,u'\}$ leaves the same digraph in $s$ and in $t$,
which is acyclic; so every directed cycle of $t$ uses the reversed edge, and
$t$ has a directed cycle iff $s$ has a directed path from the tail of
$\{u,u'\}$ to its head not using that edge. The stated example is checked
directly: $s$ is an acyclic unique sink orientation of bottom-antipodal
heights $(0,1,2,2,3,1,3,1)$, $s(1)\oplus s(5)=1\oplus5=4=e_2$, and $t$ is a
unique sink orientation containing the directed cycle $1\to5\to7\to3\to1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Drive lines, fences, cells]\label{mw:def-line}
Fix $m$ and $\delta>0$ and let $\Sigma_{m,\delta}$ be the set of one-player
reduced readout systems $\Psi=(p^{v,a},q^{v,a})_{v\le m,\,a\in\{0,1\}}$
(\Cref{lem:readout-reduce}, \Cref{def:readout-system} with $r=1$) with
$p^{v,a}\ge0$, $p^{v,a}_v=0$, $q^{v,a}\ge0$ and
$|p^{v,a}|_1+q^{v,a}\le1-\delta$; it is a convex polytope in
$\mathbb R^{2m^2}$. For $\Psi\in\Sigma_{m,\delta}$ and
$\sigma\in\{0,1\}^m$ let $P_\sigma$ be the matrix with rows $p^{v,\sigma(v)}$,
$q_\sigma$ the vector with entries $q^{v,\sigma(v)}$,
$x_\sigma:=(I-P_\sigma)^{-1}q_\sigma$ and
\[
  g_\Psi(\sigma,v)\;:=\;p^{v,1-\sigma(v)}\!\cdot x_\sigma+q^{v,1-\sigma(v)}-x_\sigma(v).
\]
$\Psi$ is \emph{nondegenerate} when no $g_\Psi(\sigma,v)$ vanishes, and then
its outmap is $s_\Psi(\sigma)=\{v:g_\Psi(\sigma,v)>0\}$. A \emph{drive line}
is a map $\Psi:[0,1]\to\Sigma_{m,\delta}$ whose coordinates are rational
functions of $t$ without poles on $[0,1]$; a \emph{fence} is a $t$ at which
$\Psi(t)$ is degenerate, and the \emph{cells} are the connected components of
the complement of the fence set. A fence $t^{\ast}$ is \emph{simple} when
exactly one cube edge is tied at it and the two gaps on that edge change sign
there.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Ties are an edge phenomenon]\label{mw:tie-edge}
For $\Psi\in\Sigma_{m,\delta}$, $\sigma\in\{0,1\}^m$ and $v\le m$, write
$\sigma':=\sigma\oplus e_v$. Then $g_\Psi(\sigma,v)=0$ if and only if
$x_\sigma=x_{\sigma'}$, if and only if $g_\Psi(\sigma',v)=0$; and otherwise
$g_\Psi(\sigma,v)$ and $g_\Psi(\sigma',v)$ are nonzero of opposite signs.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is \Cref{lem:trichotomy} in the readout language. If $g_\Psi(\sigma,v)=0$
then $x_\sigma$ satisfies $x_\sigma(w)=\Psi_{w,\sigma'(w)}(x_\sigma)$ for
every $w$, so by uniqueness of the fixed point of the contraction
$y\mapsto(\Psi_{w,\sigma'(w)}(y))_w$ we get $x_{\sigma'}=x_\sigma$, whence
$g_\Psi(\sigma',v)=0$; and symmetrically. If $g_\Psi(\sigma,v)>0$ then the
monotone map $F(y)_w:=\Psi_{w,\sigma'(w)}(y)$ satisfies $F(x_\sigma)\ge
x_\sigma$ with strict inequality at $v$, so its fixed point $x_{\sigma'}$
dominates $F(x_\sigma)$ and $x_{\sigma'}(v)>x_\sigma(v)$; were
$g_\Psi(\sigma',v)>0$ the same argument with the roles exchanged would give
$x_\sigma(v)>x_{\sigma'}(v)$, and $g_\Psi(\sigma',v)=0$ is excluded by the
first part; so $g_\Psi(\sigma',v)<0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The cell theorem]\label{mw:cells}
Let $\Psi$ be a drive line no gap of which vanishes identically.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item The fence set is finite, of cardinality at most $(m+1)m2^{m-1}$; on
      each cell the outmap $s_{\Psi(t)}$ is constant, and it lies in
      $\mathcal R_m$.
\item If $t^{\ast}$ is a simple fence with tied edge $e$, the outmaps of the
      two cells adjacent to $t^{\ast}$ differ exactly in the direction of
      $e$; both endpoints of $e$ have the same bottom-antipodal successor in
      each of the two, as \Cref{mw:flip}(b) requires.
\item Consequently, if every fence of $\Psi$ is simple, the sequence of cell
      outmaps of $\Psi$ is a walk in $W_m$, and the number of fences is at
      least $|\Delta(s_{\Psi(0)},s_{\Psi(1)})|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(a) $\det(I-P_\sigma(t))$ is a polynomial of degree at most $m$ which does not
vanish on $[0,1]$, and by Cramer $x_\sigma$ has numerator of degree at most
$m$; so $g_\Psi(\sigma,v)$ is a polynomial of degree at most $m+1$ over that
determinant, with at most $m+1$ zeros; by \Cref{mw:tie-edge} the zeros come
in edge-pairs, and the cube has $m2^{m-1}$ edges. Off the fences no gap
vanishes, so the outmap is locally constant, hence constant on a cell. That
outmap lies in $\mathcal R_m$: the conditions ``$\Psi$ realises $s$'' are
finitely many strict inequalities, so they hold on a neighbourhood inside
$\Sigma_{m,\delta/2}$, which contains dyadic systems, to which
\Cref{thm:readout-realise}(b) applies.
(b) Only the two gaps on $e$ change sign, so only $s(\sigma)$ and
$s(\sigma\oplus e_v)$ change, and each in the coordinate $v$ only: that is
the reversal of $e$. Both cell outmaps are acyclic unique sink orientations
(\Cref{prop:allsw-auso}), so \Cref{mw:flip}(a) applies.
(c) Immediate from (b) and \Cref{mw:def-graph}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Monotone drive lines]\label{mw:monotone}
Let $\Psi$ be an affine drive line for which either
(i) exactly one row $(v_0,a_0)$ of $\Psi(t)$ is non-constant, or
(ii) every $p^{v,a}$ is constant and only the $q^{v,a}$ move --- the shape of
a driven block (\Cref{def:pinned}, \Cref{rem:pinned-escape}).
Then every gap $g_{\Psi(t)}(\sigma,v)$ is a quotient of two affine functions
of $t$ with denominator of constant sign on $[0,1]$ --- affine outright in
case (ii). Hence each gap that is not identically zero vanishes at most once,
each edge of the cube is tied at most once, the fences number at most
$m2^{m-1}$, and if all of them are simple their number is \emph{exactly}
$|\Delta(s_{\Psi(0)},s_{\Psi(1)})|$: the walk in $W_m$ that the line performs
is a geodesic of $\mathcal F_m$ and no edge is reversed twice.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Case (ii): $I-P_\sigma$ is constant and invertible, so $x_\sigma(t)$ is affine
and so is $g(\sigma,v)$. Case (i): if $\sigma(v_0)\ne a_0$ then $x_\sigma$ is
constant and $g(\sigma,v)$ is constant unless $(v,1-\sigma(v))=(v_0,a_0)$,
when it is affine. If $\sigma(v_0)=a_0$, only the row $v_0$ of
$I-P_\sigma(t)$ and of $q_\sigma(t)$ moves, and affinely; expanding along it,
both Cramer determinants are affine, and the alternative rows are all
constant since $(v_0,a_0)=(v,1-\sigma(v))$ would force $\sigma(v_0)=1-a_0$.
A quotient of two affine functions with non-vanishing denominator has at most
one zero unless it is identically zero; by \Cref{mw:tie-edge} an edge is tied
exactly where either of its gaps vanishes. If every fence is simple, the
fences are in bijection with the edges reversed, each reversed once, so the
count equals $|\Delta|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[$W_3$ is connected]\label{mw:w3}
$\mathcal R_3$ is exactly the set of Holt--Klee acyclic unique sink
orientations of the $3$-cube, $656$ of the $728$ acyclic ones
(\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}, \Cref{prop:m3-realised}), and the induced subgraph
$W_3$ is connected, of minimum degree $3$, maximum degree $12$ and average
degree $5.41$; the flip graph $\mathcal F_3$ of all $728$ is connected as
well.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[What is open about $W_m$]\label{mw:open}
Is $W_m$ connected for $m\ge4$? Is every Holt--Klee class reachable in $W_m$
from the trivial orientation --- the $162$ unresolved Holt--Klee classes of
the $4$-cube of \Cref{rem:hk-survey} are exactly those no walk has reached?
And is every pair of realised systems joined by a drive line all of whose
fences are simple? The segment between two systems of $\Sigma_{m,\delta}$
lies in $\Sigma_{m,\delta}$, which is convex, and each degeneracy locus
$\{g(\sigma,v)=0\}$ is a smooth hypersurface ---
$\partial g(\sigma,v)/\partial q^{v,1-\sigma(v)}=1$ identically, that row not
entering $x_\sigma$ --- so what is missing for ``$W_m$ is connected'' is
exactly a transversality statement: that a generic segment meets no two
degeneracy loci at once. We do not prove it.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[A one-player driven block never returns]\label{mw:drive-return}
Let $G$ be stopping, $\mathfrak B\subseteq\Vmax$ with $|\mathfrak B|=m'$, and
$\beta\notin\mathfrak B$ pinned at the payoff $\theta$ (\Cref{def:readout}).
Suppose that on an interval of drive values the readouts of $\mathfrak B$ in
the pinned game form a \emph{one-player} readout system whose coefficients on
the $\mathfrak B$-values do not depend on $\theta$, only the constant terms
doing so, and affinely. Then the drive line is of type (ii) of
\Cref{mw:monotone}: every edge of the $m'$-cube ties at most once, the
block's orientation performs a walk in $\mathcal F_{m'}$ that reverses no
edge twice and therefore never returns to an orientation it has left, and the
line has at most $m'2^{m'-1}$ fences and $m'2^{m'-1}+1$ cells.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[The height-twelve orientations of the $5$-cube, and their ties]\label{mw:twelve-flat}
There are exactly $480$ acyclic unique sink orientations of the $5$-cube whose
bottom-antipodal walk from $0$ has length $12$, and none whose walk from $0$
has length $13$; so, up to translation, these are all the orientations of
bottom-antipodal height $12$, and $h^{\ast}(5)=12$ (\Cref{prop:hstar-five}).
None of the $480$ is Holt--Klee (\Cref{prop:hkfive}). For each of them
consider, as in \Cref{lem:seven-flat}, the partitions of the $5$-cube into
subcubes satisfying
(F1) $s(\sigma)\oplus s(\sigma')=\sigma\oplus\sigma'$ inside a block ---
equivalently, $\sigma\oplus s(\sigma)$ constant on a block;
(F2) $s(\sigma_t)\cap D_{A(\sigma_t)}=\emptyset$ at every walk vertex;
(F3) the quotient digraph on blocks, arcs from the non-flat $s$-edges,
acyclic;
(F4) for every face $F$ with free set $J$, the set
$\{\sigma\in F:(s(\sigma)\setminus D_{A(\sigma)})\cap J=\emptyset\}$ equal to
$A\cap F$ for a single block $A$.
Exactly $240$ of the $480$ admit a partition with a block of dimension at
least $1$; in each such case the partition is unique, its only nontrivial
block is the single edge $\{\sigma_0,\sigma_0\oplus e_x\}$ at the
\emph{start}, and the run carries exactly one flat incidence, namely
$(\sigma_0,x)$. The five values of $x$ occur $48$ times each.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A finite exhaustive computation, of the same shape as
\Cref{lem:seven-flat}'s. The $480$ orientations are produced by a depth-first
search over the walk $\sigma_0=0,\dots,\sigma_{12}$ with $s(\sigma_t)=S_t$
and $s(\sigma_{12})=0$, pruned by \Cref{cor:no-return}, \Cref{cor:law-b} and
the Szab\'o--Welzl condition among the assigned vertices (the outmap of a
unique sink orientation is a bijection), followed by a bijective completion
of the remaining $19$ vertices under that condition and an acyclicity test;
the same program at length $13$ returns nothing, which reproduces

\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One player cannot reach twelve, with or without ties]\label{mw:no-twelve}
No stopping SSG with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ and $|\Vmax|=5$ has an all-switches
run of length $12$, degenerate or not. Hence
\[
  h^{\ast}_{1}(5)\;=\;h^{\ast,\mathrm{nd}}_{1}(5)\;=\;h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{LP}}(5)
  \;=\;h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(5)\;=\;11\;<\;12\;=\;h^{\ast}(5),
\]
and the one-player row of \Cref{rem:four-ceilings} reads $1,2,4,6,11$ for
$m\le5$: ties do not beat the Holt--Klee ceiling at any $m\le5$, and the
one-player ceiling is now known exactly at every $m\le5$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $G$ is such a game with run $\sigma_0,\dots,\sigma_{12}$. Its run
vertices lie in pairwise distinct flat classes (\Cref{lem:flat-class}(c)), so
$c_{A(\sigma_t)}:=\sigma_t$ is a consistent choice of corners; extend it
arbitrarily and let $s'$ be the resolution of \Cref{thm:flat-resolution}. By
\Cref{cor:ceiling-general} the run is the bottom-antipodal walk of $s'$ from
$\sigma_0$, so $s'$ has height at least $12$, hence exactly $12$ by
$h^{\ast}(5)=12$; translating by $\sigma_0$ we may assume $\sigma_0=0$, and
then $s'$ is one of the $480$ of \Cref{mw:twelve-flat}. The flat partition of
$G$ satisfies (F1)--(F4) with respect to $s'$ and $\sigma_0$: (F1) because
$s'(\sigma)=S_A\cup(\sigma\oplus c_A)$ on a class $A$; (F2) because
$s'(\sigma_t)=S(\sigma_t)$ is disjoint from $D(\sigma_t)$; (F3) by
\Cref{lem:flat-class}(c); (F4) by \Cref{lem:face-sink}. By
\Cref{mw:twelve-flat} either every flat class is a singleton --- $G$ is
nondegenerate --- or the only nontrivial class is the edge
$\{\sigma_0,\sigma_0\oplus e_x\}$ and the run carries exactly one flat
incidence. In both cases \Cref{cor:one-tie} and \Cref{lem:tie-perturb}
produce a generic linear functional on $X(G)$ whose orientation is an acyclic
unique sink orientation satisfying Holt--Klee on every face and whose
bottom-antipodal walk from $\sigma_0$ is the run, of length $12$; so
$12\le h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(5)=11$ (\Cref{prop:hkfive}) --- a
contradiction. The displayed chain follows from
$h^{\ast,\mathrm{nd}}_{1}\le h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{LP}}\le h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}$
(\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}), from $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(5)=11$ and from the
nondegenerate witness of \Cref{prop:hstar-one-eleven}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{mw:no-twelve-scope}
Three things separate. First, the enumeration replaces the sentence after
\Cref{prop:hkfive} --- ``other height-$12$ classes of the $5$-cube exist and
cannot be enumerated'' --- which is too pessimistic: the walk-then-complete
search of that proposition's own proof enumerates all of them, $480$ with the
run starting at $0$, in about a second. Second, what is excluded is a
\emph{run} of length $12$; a degenerate game whose resolution has height $12$
while all its runs are shorter is not excluded, exactly as in
\Cref{thm:no-seven}. Third, the mechanism by which a tie could beat the
Holt--Klee ceiling is now known to be blocked in the same way at $m=4$ and at
$m=5$: at both sizes the only tie a maximal run can carry sits on a single
edge at the start, where the coordinate functional $d(y)=y_{x,a}$ of
\Cref{cor:one-tie} breaks it. At $m=6$ the argument would need the
height-$16$ orientations of the $6$-cube, which this method cannot enumerate.
\end{remark}
